lessons.title: Check, trade, then strike
lessons.sub: Bishop check, swap bishops, then your d-pawn hits back
lessons.why: The main line of the Giuoco Piano, and the one White players at your level aim for.

lessons.title: Queen takes back: grab the e-pawn
lessons.sub: The queen left the e-pawn alone; take it, then guard the knight
lessons.why: Almost four in ten club players take back with the queen here. It drops a pawn.

lessons.title: Knight blocks the check
lessons.sub: Take the e-pawn, trade, then strike with the d-pawn
lessons.why: More than half of club players block the check with the knight. That leaves their e-pawn loose.

lessons.title: Pawn hits your knight
lessons.sub: Strike back with the d-pawn
lessons.why: White pushes past instead of taking back. The answer is the same idea: your d-pawn hits back.
lessons.outcome: Equal, and your pieces are active

lessons.title: One setup for the slow Italian
lessons.sub: Small d-pawn move, a-pawn, bishop back, castle
lessons.why: The quiet d-pawn move is White's most common fourth move at your level.
lessons.outcome: Equal; you have a plan and White often doesn't

lessons.title: Knight jumps at f7: castle
lessons.sub: Castle, then kick it with the h-pawn; the sacrifice on f7 hands you two pieces for a rook
lessons.why: At your level more than a third of White players jump the knight forward as soon as the d-pawn moves.
lessons.outcome: You are better: White has moved one piece twice

lessons.title: Bishop pins your knight
lessons.sub: Ask the bishop at once with the h-pawn
lessons.why: The pin is the second most common idea White tries in the slow Italian.

lessons.title: Knight out first
lessons.sub: Same setup; the knight jump to the edge kills White's bishop
lessons.why: The four-knights version of the slow Italian. You lost two games in it, in July and in October.
lessons.outcome: Equal; you get rid of White's best bishop

lessons.title: White castles at once
lessons.sub: Same setup; take with the bishop if the d-pawn rushes
lessons.why: Castling first is White's second most common fourth move at your level.

lessons.title: The b-pawn gambit
lessons.sub: Take the pawn, tuck the bishop back, then hit the Italian bishop
lessons.why: The Evans Gambit is a fast-attack weapon. You took the pawn against CaptEvans88 and won; this is the safe way to keep it.

lessons.title: Early center push
lessons.sub: Bishop takes, then the knight, then develop
lessons.why: White gives a pawn to open lines. You take it with pieces and keep it.

lessons.title: Cheap shots at f7
lessons.sub: Count the attackers: your queen wins the knight
lessons.why: At your level these come up a few times in every hundred games. Each one loses material for White.

lessons.title: White castles: bishop out, castle
lessons.sub: Same setup as the Italian: bishop to its diagonal, castle, small d-pawn
lessons.why: About a quarter of White players castle here. You already play the bishop out against the Spanish by instinct; this makes it the rule.
lessons.outcome: About equal; the same position type as your Italian

lessons.title: Pawn guards the e-pawn
lessons.sub: Bishop out to the same diagonal as in the Italian
lessons.why: You played the bishop out against this in both of your games and won both.

lessons.title: Knight out: bishop out, castle
lessons.sub: Same setup; one trick if White grabs your e-pawn
lessons.why: The Four Knights version of the Spanish. You won with this exact setup on Oct 31.

lessons.title: Take back with the d-pawn
lessons.sub: Open lines for your queen and bishop, then win the pawn back
lessons.why: The bishop trade is the most common reply at your level. Against vasylsaienko in July you took back with the b-pawn and lost your bishop four moves later. The d-pawn recapture brings your queen and bishop out at once.
lessons.outcome: Equal; your bishops get open lines

lessons.title: Knight trade: the queen hits f2
lessons.sub: Queen out with a mate threat, the d-pawn takes back, then castle long
lessons.why: Over half of club players trade knights at once. Against maopfar and alwayssurrender31 your bishop checked first and then went back to this diagonal: a move lost. It goes there straight away.
lessons.outcome: Equal; your rook owns the open d-file

lessons.title: Bishop guards the knight: castle
lessons.sub: Queen out, the other knight behind it, castle; trade bishops if the knights come off
lessons.why: About three club players in ten guard the knight with the bishop. Six in ten then play the small c-pawn move, and the same calm setup answers everything.

lessons.title: Small c-pawn: knight out
lessons.sub: Knight hits the e-pawn; a bishop pin walks into the check on f2
lessons.why: The pawn guards the knight, but it costs White a move. Hit the e-pawn at once.

lessons.title: Knight steps back: so does the bishop
lessons.sub: Bishop back out of reach, knight out, castle
lessons.why: The knight hits your bishop, so it steps back to safety and keeps its aim at f2.

lessons.title: Bishop out instead of taking
lessons.sub: Bishop out, knight out, then the check and the d-pawn
lessons.why: Twice the c-pawn capture let White's bishop take on f7 and the queen win your bishop back with check: against themobun (2050) in July and trijhg on Oct 31. Developing the knight keeps it simple.

lessons.title: The small c-pawn gambit
lessons.sub: Hit back with your d-pawn and swap off White's knight
lessons.why: A gambit that works best when you take everything. Strike back instead.
lessons.outcome: Equal; White's center pawn is isolated

lessons.title: Queen takes back: kick it
lessons.sub: Knight hits the queen, then pin the knight and castle
lessons.why: At your level more than half of White players who push the d-pawn take back with the queen.

lessons.title: The Danish: hit back with the d-pawn
lessons.sub: Don't take the second pawn; strike the center instead
lessons.why: Three times you took the second pawn and twice White's pieces came out fast and won: against yonatha32 in October and abodeh7 on Nov 1. The d-pawn strike turns the gambit off.
lessons.outcome: Equal; White's center pawn is isolated

lessons.title: Other third moves
lessons.sub: Knight out: back in the Scotch, bishop out at once
lessons.why: Move orders that land back in positions you know.

lessons.title: The Spanish bishop: you are in your Spanish lesson
lessons.sub: The same position as your Spanish lesson: bishop out, castle, small d-pawn
lessons.why: The Spanish Four Knights is the Spanish with the knights out first. Your bishop goes to the same diagonal as always.

lessons.title: Center push: pin, then strike
lessons.sub: Take, pin the knight, then push your d-pawn
lessons.why: Two of your games went exactly this way: a win against Jaydenh625 in July, and an equal opening against Eschoir in October.

lessons.title: Bishop to the long diagonal
lessons.sub: Your Italian bishop, same plan
lessons.why: The same position as the Italian with the knights out. You won against bessauro14 from here.

lessons.title: Slow fourth moves
lessons.sub: Strike in the center with the d-pawn
lessons.why: When White wastes a move, your d-pawn takes the center for free.

lessons.title: Bishop out: knights first, then yours
lessons.sub: Knight out, then your bishop to its diagonal, then the small d-pawn
lessons.why: Against irekmary in July your bishop came out first and White's queen hit your g-pawn on move four. With the knight out first, the queen can't come, and then the bishop goes to its usual diagonal.
lessons.outcome: Equal; the same setup as your Italian

lessons.title: The Vienna Gambit: bishop out, don't take
lessons.sub: Bishop to its diagonal, small d-pawn, knight out, then the knight jumps at the Italian bishop
lessons.why: Three Vienna gambits, one win. Against Skrammande the bishop came out as here, then your own f-pawn push opened your king. Keep to the setup: bishop, small d-pawn, knight out, castle. White's king can't castle short while your bishop eyes it.
lessons.outcome: Equal; White's king has nowhere safe to go

lessons.title: Other Vienna moves
lessons.sub: Knight out and take the center
lessons.why: The other ways White develops the queen's knight first.

lessons.title: Small c-pawn move
lessons.sub: Knight takes the e-pawn; meet the push with the knight retreat
lessons.why: The Ponziani. Rare, but the knight grab leaves you comfortable.

lessons.title: Small d-pawn move
lessons.sub: Knight out, then strike with the d-pawn
lessons.why: Slow moves give you the center for free.

lessons.title: Odd third moves
lessons.sub: Two of them lose material
lessons.why: Rare tries. The knight grab simply drops a piece.

lessons.title: Queen hits f7 twice
lessons.sub: Pawn blocks, knight blocks, then castle or jump into the center
lessons.why: You lost twice to this on Oct 14, against GambitTwojejKozy and Nona_Zulfa. Both times your bishop went to the Italian diagonal and White's queen and bishop won your knight. The bishop belongs next to your king.

lessons.title: Other queen moves
lessons.sub: Knight out with a threat every time
lessons.why: Early queen moves come up a few times in every hundred games at your level.

lessons.title: Bishop out, don't take
lessons.sub: Bishop to its diagonal stops White castling; small d-pawn, both knights out, then the knight jumps at White's bishop
lessons.why: Three King's Gambits, one win: against TiepiMT the knight went behind the pawns and you lost on time, and against tbergosmede on Nov 1 your knight went back home on move three. The bishop on its usual diagonal keeps White's king in the middle, and if the pawn grabs your e-pawn, the queen check wins a rook.

lessons.title: Bishop out on move two
lessons.sub: Knight out; back to your Italian or the center grab
lessons.why: Four of your games started this way, three of them against JChav3z on Oct 29. The two losses came after an early edge-pawn move; knight out, then the bishop, won. Most move orders lead back to the Italian or the Vienna.

lessons.title: E-pawn against the c-pawn
lessons.sub: Knights out, bishop at the knight, then push the e-pawn
lessons.why: You beat Mahm00dsaad with the e-pawn reply in October.

lessons.title: Other second moves
lessons.sub: Same e-pawn, then the d-pawn strike
lessons.why: The fianchetto is the next most common second move.

lessons.title: Knight out first
lessons.sub: D-pawn to the middle, then your Slav setup
lessons.why: Against the king's knight first, the d-pawn goes to the middle and the same Slav setup follows.

lessons.title: King's fianchetto first
lessons.sub: E-pawn two squares, then the d-pawn
lessons.why: Against Server_goat9 in July a pawn move took a guard away from your knight, and the long-diagonal bishop and queen won it. Keep your knight guarded.

lessons.title: Small e-pawn first
lessons.sub: E-pawn two squares, then the d-pawn
lessons.why: If the e-pawn later goes forward a second time, you are simply a move ahead, as in your bullet game against shiblifx1.

lessons.title: Queen's fianchetto
lessons.sub: Knight guards your e-pawn, then the d-pawn
lessons.why: The Nimzo-Larsen. Guard the e-pawn with the knight and take the center.

lessons.title: The f-pawn first
lessons.sub: D-pawn two squares, knight out, then your bishop: the same setup as against the d-pawn
lessons.why: The Bird. The f-pawn weakens White's king a little; develop normally.

lessons.title: Edge moves and the b-pawn
lessons.sub: Take the center; the b-pawn can be grabbed
lessons.why: These come up once in a long while. Take the center and develop.

lessons.title: Small e-pawn: bishop out at once
lessons.sub: Bishop, e-pawn, queen's knight, king's knight; trade White's bishop when it comes
lessons.why: About one Queen's Gambit player in seven at your level guards the c-pawn with the small e-pawn move. Nothing stops your bishop.

lessons.title: Knights out, then the small e-pawn
lessons.sub: Same setup, same squares: bishop, e-pawn, queen's knight, dark bishop, castle
lessons.why: The most common way White reaches the small e-pawn position. Every piece goes where it went in the first lesson.

lessons.title: Both knights out: take the c-pawn
lessons.sub: Take, hold it with the b-pawn, and grab the e-pawn if the knight runs to the edge
lessons.why: The main line of the Slav. Three in four players at your level push the e-pawn here instead of the edge pawn; then your b-pawn holds the extra pawn.

lessons.title: Pawn trade: knight beside the d-pawn
lessons.sub: Take back with the c-pawn, knight to its square, bishop out
lessons.why: About one in ten Queen's Gambit players trade at once. The position is symmetrical, your pieces copy White's, and the game stays calm.

lessons.title: Bishop comes at your knight: jump to the middle
lessons.sub: Knight jump; if White moves the e-pawn, the queen check wins the bishop
lessons.why: A quarter of club players bring the bishop out at your knight here, and three in four of them then play the natural e-pawn move that loses the bishop.

lessons.title: Bishop to the long diagonal: take the c-pawn
lessons.sub: Take, hold it with the b-pawn, then the e-pawn
lessons.why: Once White's dark bishop has left, your queen and knight can hit the squares it no longer guards. Take the c-pawn.

lessons.title: Copy the bishop
lessons.sub: Bishop out, e-pawn, trade White's other bishop, then offer the dark one
lessons.why: Mirror White, trade both bishops, and the game is equal and calm. In July this setup beat a London player in fourteen moves.

lessons.title: The c-pawn push: same bishop offer
lessons.sub: E-pawn, offer the dark bishops, queen takes back, then the c-pawn guards your d-pawn
lessons.why: About one London player in ten pushes the c-pawn early. Nothing changes: offer the bishop trade, take back with the queen, and guard the d-pawn with the c-pawn.

lessons.title: Knight out first
lessons.sub: Same plan: bishop out, e-pawn, trade the bishops
lessons.why: A fifth of London players bring the knight out first. Same squares for every piece.

lessons.title: Knight in front of the c-pawn
lessons.sub: Same setup; when the knight jumps at your c-pawn, guard it from the edge
lessons.why: A third of club players jump the knight at your c-pawn the very next move. Guard it with the knight from the edge.

lessons.title: Bishop out before White's bishop
lessons.sub: Trade bishops, then the c-pawn, the e-pawn, the queen's knight and the dark bishop
lessons.why: The Colle is the quiet system club players love. With your bishop out first, its best attacking piece gets traded, and your pawns and pieces go where they go in the Slav.

lessons.title: King's knight out, then the bishop
lessons.sub: Jump the knight at the bishop, then bring your bishop out
lessons.why: About one club player in eight brings the bishop out at your knight after the king's knight comes out. The knight jump makes White decide at once.

lessons.title: Queen's knight out, then the bishop
lessons.sub: Bishop out; if White takes the knight, take back with the e-pawn
lessons.why: About one club player in five brings the bishop out at your knight here. Taking back with the e-pawn keeps your king safe and your dark bishop free.

lessons.title: The e-pawn gambit
lessons.sub: Take the pawn, bring the bishop out, keep the extra pawn or return it with a better game
lessons.why: A rare gambit, but the players who use it play it every game. Taking and developing is all you need.

lessons.title: Odd second moves
lessons.sub: Same setup against everything
lessons.why: Rare second moves. Your pieces still go to the same squares.

lessons.title: The open game
lessons.sub: A-pawn, queen, knight, then the b-pawn
lessons.why: Half your games start with the knight, and half of those open the middle. The same six moves answer every version.

lessons.title: Bishop out on move two
lessons.sub: E-pawn blocks it, d-pawn hits it
lessons.why: One opponent in six plays the Italian bishop against everything. Here it runs into a wall and loses a move.

lessons.title: The small c-pawn
lessons.sub: D-pawn two squares, then pile up on the d-pawn
lessons.why: About one game in ten. You already know the plan from playing White against the French: hit the pawn that holds the chain.

lessons.title: D-pawn on move two
lessons.sub: Take it; the knight hits the queen
lessons.why: One in twelve. The queen comes out too early and your knight gains a move on her.

lessons.title: F-pawn on move two
lessons.sub: E-pawn, then the d-pawn two squares
lessons.why: Slow attacking setups. The d-pawn in the middle takes the sting out of all of them.

lessons.title: The e-pawn pushes past
lessons.sub: Bishop out, e-pawn, then the c-pawn two squares
lessons.why: Half the club players who put both pawns in the middle push the e-pawn past. Your bishop is already outside the chain, which is the whole point of this opening.

lessons.title: The pawn trade
lessons.sub: Take back with the c-pawn, both knights, then the bishop
lessons.why: One in four trades pawns on move three. You get the open c-file and an easy game.

lessons.title: The c-pawn attacks your d-pawn
lessons.sub: Knight out, then guard the d-pawn with the e-pawn
lessons.why: About one in ten follows the trade with the c-pawn. This is the one line where the bishop stays home: the d-pawn needs the e-pawn at once.
lessons.outcome: Equal; White has a lone d-pawn to defend

lessons.title: Take, then the bishop out
lessons.sub: Bishop out, step back, queen's knight, e-pawn
lessons.why: The oldest main line. A third of club players then guard the knight with the bishop, and that loses the d-pawn.
lessons.outcome: Equal; a pawn up if White slips

lessons.title: Both knights out
lessons.sub: Bishop out at the knight, then the e-pawn
lessons.why: A fifth of your games will start with a knight on move two. When both knights are out your bishop has a target.

lessons.title: Bishop out on move two
lessons.sub: D-pawn hits it and you gain a move
lessons.why: One in nine brings the Italian bishop out against this too. Your d-pawn arrives with a hit on it.

lessons.title: F-pawn or a slow d-pawn
lessons.sub: The same two pawn moves, then the bishop
lessons.why: These come up now and then. Nothing changes: two pawn moves, then the bishop.

parts.title: White builds the big center
parts.blurb: White prepares the d-pawn push with the small c-pawn move. Take, check, trade bishops, then hit back in the center with your own d-pawn.

parts.title: The slow Italian
parts.blurb: White keeps the center closed and develops. You use one setup against all of it, and you watch out for the early knight jump at f7.

parts.title: Gambits and cheap shots
parts.blurb: Early pawn sacrifices and lunges at f7. Each one has a calm answer that leaves you better.

parts.title: White castles
parts.blurb: White castles and leaves the e-pawn to its fate. Ignore it: your bishop goes to the same diagonal as in the Italian and you castle too.

parts.title: Quiet fourth moves
parts.blurb: White guards the e-pawn and develops. Your bishop goes to the same diagonal as in the Italian.

parts.title: Bishop takes your knight
parts.blurb: White trades the bishop for your knight. Take back toward the center, then win your pawn back.

parts.title: Knight takes back
parts.blurb: White trades in the center and takes back with the knight. Your bishop goes straight to its Italian diagonal and the queen joins it against f2.

parts.title: White gives a pawn
parts.blurb: White leaves your extra pawn alone to develop fast. Develop with tempo and hit back in the center.

parts.title: The d-pawn on move two
parts.blurb: White pushes the d-pawn before the knight comes out. Take, then either kick the queen or decline the gambit with your own d-pawn.

parts.title: Four Knights
parts.blurb: White brings the other knight out on move three. Copy the pin, take the center, or slide into the Italian setup you already know.

parts.title: Knight out on move two
parts.blurb: White develops the queen's knight first, often to push the f-pawn. Meet the bishop with the knight jump and the gambit with a pawn of your own.

parts.title: Quiet third moves
parts.blurb: Slow moves like the small d-pawn or c-pawn. Hit the center with your d-pawn as soon as it is safe.

parts.title: The early queen
parts.blurb: White brings the queen out on move two to aim at f7. Guard with the pawn and knight, then kick the queen around with tempo.

parts.title: The f-pawn gambit
parts.blurb: White offers the f-pawn to rip open the f-file. Take it, then hit back in the center with your d-pawn.

parts.title: Bishop out on move two
parts.blurb: White puts the bishop on the f7 diagonal before the knight. Most of the time you are back in the Italian.

parts.title: The c-pawn first
parts.blurb: White starts with the c-pawn. Play the e-pawn two squares, as you would against the e-pawn, and develop the knights.

parts.title: Knight or fianchetto first
parts.blurb: Against the knight, use your Queen's Gambit setup; against the g-pawn fianchetto, take the center with the e-pawn.

parts.title: Rare first moves
parts.blurb: Small pawn moves and edge moves. Take the center and develop, and punish the ones that weaken White's king.

parts.title: The small e-pawn move
parts.blurb: White guards the c-pawn with the small e-pawn move. Your bishop comes out before your e-pawn, and the same pieces go to the same squares every game.

parts.title: Both knights out
parts.blurb: With both White knights out, your bishop cannot come out safely yet. Take the c-pawn first and hold it with the b-pawn; the bishop follows.

parts.title: White trades pawns
parts.blurb: White takes on your d-pawn. Take back with the c-pawn, put the queen's knight beside it and bring the bishop out again.

parts.title: White's bishop comes out early
parts.blurb: White's dark bishop leaves before the e-pawn moves. When the bishop comes out at your knight, jump the knight to the middle; against the long-diagonal bishop, take the c-pawn.

parts.title: Bishop out before the e-pawn
parts.blurb: White's bishop comes out first. Yours comes out too, then the e-pawn, and your dark bishop offers to trade off the London bishop.

parts.title: The knight joins the bishop
parts.blurb: White adds the queen's knight beside the bishop. One trick to know: the knight jump at your c-pawn.

parts.title: Small e-pawn systems
parts.blurb: White builds a quiet pawn triangle and aims the bishop at your king. Get your bishop out first, trade it, then build the same triangle as in the Slav: c-pawn, e-pawn, queen's knight, dark bishop, castle.

parts.title: Bishop comes at your knight
parts.blurb: White's bishop comes out at your knight early. Jump the knight forward when the middle square is free; otherwise carry on with the setup and take back with the e-pawn if White takes.

parts.title: E-pawn gambits
parts.blurb: White offers the e-pawn to open lines. Take it, develop, and give back nothing.

parts.title: Odd second moves
parts.blurb: Rare moves. Same setup.

parts.title: White opens the middle
parts.blurb: White trades the d-pawn for your c-pawn. You get a half-open c-file and two middle pawns; the small a-pawn move keeps knights and bishops off your queenside.

parts.title: The bishop comes out early
parts.blurb: The most common mistake against the Sicilian at club level. Your e-pawn blocks the bishop and the d-pawn hits it.

parts.title: White builds a center first
parts.blurb: White wants two pawns in the middle. Your d-pawn goes two squares at once, and the game looks like a French where your bad bishop has more room.

parts.title: Other second moves
parts.blurb: The d-pawn at once, or the f-pawn. Develop with a hit on the queen, or put the d-pawn in the middle.

parts.title: White pushes past
parts.blurb: White's e-pawn steps past your d-pawn. Bishop out first, then the e-pawn, then the c-pawn hits the base of the chain.

parts.title: White trades pawns
parts.blurb: White takes your d-pawn. Take back with the c-pawn, then both knights before the bishop, exactly as in the Slav pawn-trade lesson.

parts.title: White lets you take
parts.blurb: White guards the e-pawn with a knight. Take it, bring the bishop out with a hit on the knight, and step back when it is chased.

parts.title: Both knights, no d-pawn
parts.blurb: White brings both knights out and holds the d-pawn back. Your bishop goes to the other side and takes the knight when asked.

parts.title: Other second moves
parts.blurb: A bishop, the f-pawn or a slow d-pawn on move two. The d-pawn goes two squares all the same.

games.title: The bishop that hung three times
games.summary: White's bishop came out on move two and stayed on its square with nothing guarding it. Three times in four moves your queen could have taken it. You won material anyway and were winning for twenty moves, until a queen move left your back rank open.

games.title: A piece up, then the back rank
games.summary: Against the London your knight jumped to the middle on move three. When White's c-pawn move left the b-pawn loose you took in the center first and grabbed it a move later. A White bishop blunder put you a piece up, and you stayed far ahead until a rook move left your back rank open.

games.title: The pawn push that lost the knight
games.summary: Your knight came out on move four. White kicked it with the e-pawn and you pinned the pawn with your queen, correctly. Then White's queen broke the pin, you pushed the d-pawn, and the pawn took your knight. In the guide the bishop comes out on move four instead, and this position never arises.

games.title: Early queen, wrong bishop square
games.summary: White's queen came out on move two. You blocked f7 correctly, but your bishop went to the Italian diagonal, and then an edge pawn and a knight trip cost three moves while your king stayed in the middle. White's queen and bishop then ganged up on your knight.

games.title: The Danish, and two loose White pieces
games.summary: You took the second gambit pawn, which is playable. Then the knight jump to the edge would have hit White's queen and bishop at once, and later a White knight was left with no guard. You were clearly better twice and lost on time.

games.title: Wrong pawn, then a loose bishop
games.summary: White traded the bishop for your knight and you took back with the b-pawn. Four moves later White's knight attacked your bishop, you pushed the d-pawn, and the bishop was gone.

games.title: A free bishop, then the open h-file
games.summary: White put a bishop where your h-pawn could take it, and you took it: a whole piece up. Then your king's knight stepped back, the h-file opened, and two slips let White's queen and knights in.

games.title: The queen jump you missed four times
games.summary: Another London where the knight jumped to the middle and the queen gave an early check. Much later your knight was hitting the square beside White's king. Four moves running, the queen jump beside it threatened mate and won material; each time something else was played, and the game was lost on the clock.

games.title: The mate you didn't see
games.summary: A slow Italian. Late in the game your queen, rook and knight were all aimed at White's king. The queen sacrifice on the knight next to the king led to a forced mate; instead your knight grabbed a pawn, and White's queen got in first.

games.title: Your best win: the slow Italian, done right
games.summary: A ten-minute game against a 1769. White castled early and played slowly. You set up with the small d-pawn move, pinned the knight, prepared the d-pawn break with the c-pawn, and won a pawn when White's queen stepped off its guard.

games.title: Checkmate in fifteen moves
games.summary: White traded pawns in the center and you took back with the e-pawn. Your c-pawn and d-pawn rolled forward, a queen check won a piece, and the queen finished with checkmate on f2.

puzzles.title: The loose bishop
puzzles.t: Nothing guards White's bishop. Your queen takes it for free.

puzzles.title: Still loose
puzzles.t: Three moves later the same bishop is still hanging. Take it.

puzzles.title: Make your back rank safe
puzzles.t: White's rooks are lined up and your king has no square. A pawn move in front of the king, or a rook that guards the back rank, keeps you winning.
puzzles.q: Your back rank is weak. Find a move that keeps you winning.

puzzles.title: The free b-pawn
puzzles.t: White's small c-pawn move left the b-pawn without a guard, and taking it also hits the knight and the rook.

puzzles.title: Keep the rook on the back rank
puzzles.t: White's bishop hits your rook. Move it along the back rank, not off it, and White's rook check is harmless. You stay a piece up.
puzzles.q: Your rook is attacked. Find a move that keeps you winning.

puzzles.title: Move the knight first
puzzles.t: The pawn is about to take your knight. The jump to the middle keeps everything.

puzzles.title: Castle away from f7
puzzles.t: White's queen and bishop aim at f7. Castling takes the king out of the attack.

puzzles.title: Knight hits queen and bishop
puzzles.t: The knight jump to the edge attacks White's queen and bishop at once.

puzzles.title: The loose knight
puzzles.t: White's bishop just left the knight with no guard. Your queen takes it.

puzzles.title: Your bishop is attacked
puzzles.t: White's knight hits your bishop. Save it, or grab the e-pawn first.

puzzles.title: Queen joins the knight
puzzles.t: Your knight already hits the square next to White's king. The queen jump beside it threatens mate and wins material.

puzzles.title: Still there
puzzles.t: Two moves later the same jump is still the best move.

puzzles.title: The queen sacrifice
puzzles.t: Your queen takes the knight next to White's king. If the pawn takes back, your knight checks and your rook mates.

chapters.cap: Your d-pawn hits the bishop and the e-pawn at once.
chapters.headline: Mirror the bishop, then strike back.
chapters.lede: Your bishop goes to the same diagonal as White's, aimed at f2. If White builds the big center, check, trade bishops and hit back with your d-pawn. If White goes slow, use one setup every time and castle before the knight can jump at f7.

chapters.name: Queen's Gambit
chapters.cap: Bishop out first, then the e-pawn closes the chain behind it.

chapters.headline: Bishop out, then the e-pawn.
chapters.lede: Guard the d-pawn with the c-pawn, bring the light bishop out, then close the chain with the e-pawn. If both White knights are out, take the c-pawn first and hold it with the b-pawn.

Against the knight jump at your c-pawn, guard it from the edge.
